rules.title: The base fee level is 256 for a single-signed reference transaction
Fee level is fee paid times 256 divided by the base fee
A zero base fee is replaced by a non-zero substitute so the fee level stays non-zero; a non-positive effective fee pays fee level 0
A multi-signed transaction's base fee is the base fee plus one base fee per signer
Fee level, not drops, decides queue order: a multi-signed transaction paying more drops can rank below a cheaper single-signed one
The escalation multiplier is the median fee level of the last closed ledger, floored at the minimum escalation multiplier
The minimum escalation multiplier is the base level times 500, i.e. 128,000
Above the target, the required fee level is multiplier times current squared over target squared: quadratic, not exponential
The in-tree documentation says the fee level 'increases exponentially', but the code computes a quadratic
A series fee level sums the squares over the series; sums at or above 2^21 transactions are treated as overflow

When healthy, the expected ledger size grows fast (up to the largest recent count plus 20%) and shrinks slowly (90% of the way toward it); slow consensus cuts it by 50% and clears the recent-count buffer
Ledger-size defaults: minimum 32 transactions per ledger (1,000 standalone), target 256, optional maximum
On a slow-consensus ledger the expected size is clamped between the minimum and the previous expectation reduced by the slow-consensus percentage
Load constants: normal load factor 256, raise and lower steps of 1/4, maximum load factor 256,000,000
The local load fee rises only after two consecutive overload signals, by one quarter each time, capped at the maximum
Lowering the local load fee resets the overload count, decreases by one quarter, and never goes below the normal factor
The load factor is the maximum of the local, remote, and cluster factors; the scaling factors pair the local/remote and remote/cluster maxima
Load scaling multiplies the fee by the factor over 256; a privileged submitter pays the remote factor while the local factor is below four times remote
The load manager raises the local fee while the job queue is overloaded and lowers it otherwise
The queue is ordered by fee level descending; equal fee levels order by transaction ID XOR the parent ledger hash
The maximum queue size is the larger of expected ledgers times ledgers-in-queue and the minimum queue size; it is not updated on slow-consensus ledgers
The minimum processing fee level is the lowest queued fee level plus one when the queue is full, else the base level
One account may queue at most 10 transactions, except when filling an expiration-based sequence gap
A transaction with a LastLedgerSequence must promise at least 2 ledgers past the open ledger to be queueable
Transactions carrying PreviousTxnID or AccountTxnID, or submitted with tapFAIL_HARD, can never be queued
Blockers queue alone or by replacing the lone queued transaction; sequence numbers must be next or fill the first gap; ticket transactions need the ticket already in the ledger
A replacement must pay strictly more than the old fee level plus 25%
Queued fees in flight are bounded by the account balance and, when the reserve exceeds ten times the base fee, by the reserve
The queue drains highest fee level first and stops at the first transaction below the required level
A sequence-based transaction that is not the first for its account is skipped until its predecessor applies

A queued transaction gets 10 retry attempts; an account whose transaction retried out gives its other transactions at most 2 attempts, and a failed or expired transaction marks the account for dropping when the queue is 95% full
Transactions whose LastLedgerSequence has passed are removed when a ledger closes, and the account is marked with the drop penalty
When the queue is full, a newcomer is admitted only if its fee level beats the lowest-fee account's average fee level; that account's cheapest transaction is dropped
A new transaction can rescue a stuck account queue if the summed fee levels of the queued series plus itself cover the escalated series level; the queued transactions are then applied first
Direct apply needs the transaction sequence to match the account sequence (or a ticket) and a fee level at or above the required level; applying removes any queued transaction it replaces
The metrics report queue size, queue maximum, open-ledger size, expected size, reference level, minimum processing level, median level, and open-ledger level
The fee RPC returns levels and drops; the open-ledger fee is rounded up by one drop when the drop value would fall below the required level
Every queue setting is configurable in the transaction_queue section; the increase percentage is clamped to 0-1000 and the decrease percentage to 0-100

external.quote: The transaction cost is not paid to any party: the XRP is irrevocably destroyed.

rules.title: Transaction fees are destroyed, not paid to anyone

external.quote: If you submit a transaction through an admin connection, the server applies and relays the transaction as long as the transaction meets the un-scaled minimum transaction cost.

rules.title: A transaction submitted through an admin connection bypasses load scaling and needs only the un-scaled minimum fee

external.quote: A transaction is very unlikely to survive the consensus process unless its Fee value meets the requirements of a majority of servers.

rules.title: A transaction is very unlikely to survive consensus unless its fee meets the requirements of a majority of servers

external.quote: When the FeeEscalation amendment is enabled, there are two thresholds for the transaction cost

rules.title: With fee escalation enabled there are two thresholds: a load-based cost below which the server ignores the transaction, and an open-ledger cost below which it queues the transaction
Fee-spike threshold: the minimum fee level to enter the open ledger at a given load equals the threshold table (quadratic in the open-ledger count)
Queue-saturation eviction threshold: a newcomer must beat the lowest-fee account's average fee level to displace its cheapest transaction
Live network fee behaviour under real load: actual fee levels paid, queue occupancy, and validator divergence in production
